newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes weaker on dlr short covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes weaker on dlr short covering.

text.p: The won ended Thursday's session weaker against the dollar after hitting another monthly low as some dealers scurried to cover their short dollar positions, traders said.

The won finished at 889.20 against Wednesday's close of 888.50 falling for the third consecutive day. After opening at 888.90, it immediately rose to the day's high of 888.60, but later dropped to new monthly low of 889.50.
A dealer at Korea First Bank said a South Korean electronics company bought $100 million to cover its position.
"Dollar buying sentiment remains strong. But it is unlikely for the dollar to rise above the 890 won level tomorrow," the Korea First Bank dealer said.
Dealers forecast dollar supply would grow next week as about $300-$400 million worth of foreign funds were expected to flow in for investment in the local stock market.
Anticipation of dollar influx from the sales of depositary receipts issued by the Housing and Commerical Bank this month would also pressure the market, they said.
Friday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 888.00 down from 887.70 today. -- JANE LEE (822) 727-5648
